If the Swiss vote for UBI, what what will some of the unintended consequences be?

Higher taxes. Though I'm not sure if it has been proposed before, it doesn't seem like something they would vote for.

It takes a lot more people to pass a law than it does to propose it. For example, EU membership has been proposed and rejected multiple times. It will be interesting to see how this goes.
Higher taxes, indeed... but there is a silver lining for businesses: higher consumer spending, guaranteed.

It's a similar issue to the minimum wage. Either people spend more on more things because they have more money, stimulating the economy, or business raise their prices because they know that everyone will have at least 2,000 francs every month.
There won't necessary be any, because the UBI could end up being very small to begin with. I don't think any particular level of payment is mandated.
IIRC it is 2,000 francs (about 2,000 USD), so not exactly small. It would most likely result in much higher taxes for the top. This is one of the reasons I'm skeptical of its success.
